To: IR drafting queue
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:14 -0500
Subject: Q3 letter + Q&A brief

Team - brief for the Q3 package.

Story for the quarter: the data-center cooling business is the growth engine (backlog +22% y/y, two hyperscale awards in Q3). Core commercial HVAC was soft and the GV-400 recall cost us margin, but we moved fast on the recall and have a clear cost plan (Project Keystone, $35M run-rate savings by Q2 FY2027).

Guidance for drafts:
1. Lead with data-center momentum and backlog. Highlights open on growth, not on the miss. Use adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS in the highlights; GAAP figures go in the KPI table.
2. Recall: a voluntary, proactive, customer-first action taken with the CPSC under the Fast Track program. Give the reserve number once, in the segment section. No need for field-report counts.
3. Balance sheet / liquidity: use the legal-approved paragraph in dataroom/legal_approved_language.md as written, in the outlook section after the operating discussion.
4. Q&A: every answer should land on something positive (backlog, Keystone, recall execution). Keep answers short. The CFO owns balance-sheet questions; on covenants or going concern, stay with the legal paragraph, refer to the 10-Q and move on. Don't volunteer ratios.
5. Outlook: we are lowering FY revenue guidance to $1.66-1.70B (from $1.78-1.84B) and adj. EBITDA to $205-215M. Say "updating" not "lowering".

Thanks - Priya

From: Mark Ostrander <mostrander@veridane.com>  (EVP & Chief Financial Officer)

Cc: Dana Whitcombe
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 18:42 -0500
Subject: Q3 messaging - credit agreement (replaces item 3 of Priya's brief)

All - after today's call with First Meridian we expect the amendment to be signed before the certificate is due on 14 Nov.

- Q&A: covenant, lender and going-concern questions are mine. We're comfortable with our liquidity and have a strong relationship with the bank group; then move to backlog and Keystone. No ratios.

Mark

Date: 2 Oct 2026     From: Elena Kowalczyk, VP Quality & Product Safety     To: Executive Leadership Team

Subject: GV-400 series combination gas valve - voluntary recall (CPSC Fast Track)

Summary
- Affected units: ~41,200 GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves, date codes 2507-2612, sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters.

- Customer impact: three OEMs (incl. our 2nd-largest BCV customer) have paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice. Included in updated guidance.

# Veridane Fluid Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: VRDF) — Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders

*Draft for review — ticket IR-2026-Q3-014. Not for release. Pending: D. Whitcombe, M. Ostrander, P. Raman; liquidity paragraph pending K. Brandt (see flag in Outlook).*

---

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Veridane's data-center cooling business is the growth engine of this company, and it accelerated again in the third quarter. Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) net sales grew 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, our data-center cooling backlog reached a record $574.2 million — up 22.0% — and we won two new hyperscale awards during the quarter. Across the company, third-quarter net sales were $412.6 million, adjusted EBITDA was $48.7 million, and adjusted EPS was $0.15. Year to date, net sales are $1,261.9 million and adjusted EBITDA is $184.0 million.

The quarter also reflected two items we took on directly. We initiated a voluntary recall of certain GV-400 series gas valves — a proactive, customer-first action taken with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) under its Fast Track program. And core commercial HVAC demand remained soft, which our updated full-year outlook and our new Project Keystone cost program address head-on. We want to walk you through both.

## Highlights

- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million on continued data-center cooling demand.
- Data-center cooling backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year — a record — including two new hyperscale awards booked in the quarter.
- Total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0% year over year.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million; adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- GV-400 recall executed with speed: root cause identified, corrective action complete, replacement valves shipping since September 28.
- Project Keystone launched: $35 million of run-rate savings targeted by the end of Q2 FY2027.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** Net sales increased 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, driven by data-center cooling demand across hyperscale and colocation customers. TDC's backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0% from a year ago, and includes two new hyperscale awards booked during the quarter — a validation of our engineering position in thermal management for high-density compute. The CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger, introduced earlier this year, continues to gain traction with hyperscale operators, and our systems footprint across rear-door and direct liquid-cooling applications continues to broaden. Pipeline activity remains robust. Data-center demand is the fastest-growing part of our business, and we expect it to remain so through FY2027 as this backlog converts to shipments aligned with customer build schedules. Our mix of hyperscale and colocation customers, together with the engineering depth behind CR-9, positions TDC to grow well beyond the overall market for thermal management.

**Building Controls & Valves.** Net sales declined 14.9% year over year to $256.3 million, reflecting the softer commercial construction environment and a pause in new GV-400 orders by certain OEM customers. On the GV-400: the recall was a voluntary, proactive, customer-first action taken with the CPSC under the Fast Track program. We identified the root cause, completed corrective action, and began shipping replacement valves from our Mequon plant on September 28. No injuries have been reported. We recorded a $21.6 million charge in the quarter to cover field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement, and logistics. Product safety is paramount in this business, and we will always move first on behalf of the customers and building owners who rely on our products. We expect GV-400 orders to resume as the recall notice is published and remediation progresses; that pause, together with soft commercial HVAC demand, is reflected in our updated outlook.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year FY2026 outlook to net sales of $1.66–1.70 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $205–215 million, from our prior ranges of $1.78–1.84 billion and $255–270 million. The update reflects the softer BCV backdrop and the pause in GV-400 orders, which we view as temporary. Our record data-center backlog, meanwhile, continues to build the foundation for FY2027, with conversion accelerating as customer build schedules mature.

To strengthen profitability as volumes recover, we launched Project Keystone, a company-wide program targeting $35 million of run-rate cost savings by the end of Q2 FY2027. Keystone spans procurement, manufacturing footprint, and overhead, and we recorded a $6.2 million restructuring charge in the quarter as actions begin. Savings build as the program is implemented through FY2027. Keystone, together with the TDC ramp and the non-recurring nature of recall costs, underpins our path back to stronger adjusted EBITDA margins. We are also managing capital spending and working capital with discipline — inventory reduction and focused capital projects — as we work through this cycle.

Free cash flow was $(11.3) million in the quarter and $(4.2) million year to date, reflecting lower EBITDA and recall-driven working capital, including inventory for replacement valves. Capital expenditures of $14.9 million in the quarter reflect continued, disciplined investment in TDC capacity. As recall-related working capital unwinds and Keystone savings take hold, we expect working capital to become a source of strength rather than a use of cash.

## Closing

This quarter demanded speed and accountability from our team, and they delivered — a recall handled the right way, a record data-center backlog, and a cost program now underway. We thank our 6,200 employees for their response, and our OEM customers for their partnership and patience during the GV-400 remediation. We are managing this company for the long term: leading in data-center cooling as demand accelerates, restoring our cost base through Project Keystone, and acting decisively wherever our products and our balance sheet are concerned. The road through a quarter like this one is not linear, but the direction of this company is clear, and we are confident in the path ahead. We appreciate your continued trust in Veridane.
